name: Example - System Monitor
instruction: Send an email to your_email@example.com regarding the system state. Talk as your AI assistant persona, like an assistant notifying the user. No need to notify the main session. - **To:** your_email@example.com - **Subject:** Systema Auxilium — System State Report - **Format:** HTML (the `--html` flag is required) - **Template:** data/templates/system_state_email.html ## How to send 1. Read the HTML template from `data/templates/system_state_email.html`. 2. Substitute these EXACT strings — they are the only placeholders the template contains, and any you miss are mailed out literally: `{{report_date}}`, `{{cpu_rows}}`, `{{memory_rows}}`, `{{disk_rows}}`, `{{process_rows}}`, `{{summary}}`. - **{{report_date}}** — current date and time, e.g. "August 7, 2026 — 4:30 PM". - **{{cpu_rows}}** — CPU model, core count, usage %, uptime, as stat rows: ``` Model Example CPU ``` Use class="ok" / "warn" / "danger" by load (ok <60%, warn 60-85%, danger >85%). Those three are the ONLY status classes the template styles — anything else renders unstyled. - **{{memory_rows}}** — total RAM, used, free, usage %. Same row format. - **{{disk_rows}}** — per-drive free/total and usage %. Same row format. - **{{process_rows}}** — heaviest processes BY NAME with their memory use, not raw PIDs or command lines. Keep it readable. - **{{summary}}** — one or two sentences in plain English, e.g. "All systems nominal — CPU at 12%, RAM at 34%, nothing concerning." 3. Send it, passing the rendered HTML as the body: ``` python e_mailman.py --account "your-account-label" send \n --to "your_email@example.com" \n --subject "Systema Auxilium — System State Report" \n --body "" --html ``` System Current State: {{current_system_state()}}
